 Oral Judgment

(PER: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE P SREE SUDHA)
1.

This appeal is filed by the claimant/owner of vehicle bearing No.KA-25/MA-6029, against the Judgment and award dated 04.02.2023 passed in MVC No.326/2018 by the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT VI, Vijayapura (for short 'the tribunal') seeking enhancement of the award amount.

2. The Cruiser Jeep bearing registration No.KA- 25/MA-6029 driven by one Yashwant Hebasur met with accident on 10.12.2017, as such the owner/claimant filed claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.4,00,000/- to the NC: 2025:KHC-K:6575 HC-KAR damages to the vehicle.
The tribunal after considering the evidence on record, awarded a sum of Rs.2,30,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

Aggrieved by the said Judgment and award, the claimant preferred an appeal and mainly contended that, as per the IMV report i.e. Ex.P.4, the vehicle was damaged with respect to Front wind shield glass broken, dash board damaged, engine bonnet damaged, front both side headlights and indicators broken, front bumper damaged, radiator and radiator grill was damaged, wiper blade was broken and rear left side by was pressed inside and other damages.
He produced motor survey report under Ex.P.10.

The total estimated cost of the repair is Rs.37,22,848/-, but the tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.2,30,000/-
along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

sentences.text: The main contention of the learned counsel for the claimant/appellant is that, the surveyor is appointed by the Insurance company and the policy was in existence as on the date of the accident.

Therefore, the tribunal instead of NC: 2025:KHC-K:6575 HC-KAR relying upon Ex.P.10(a) awarded an amount of Rs.2,30,000/- which is on the lower side and thus requested for enhancement of the compensation.
The claimant examined Administrative Officer of the Insurance Company.
In the cross-examination he stated that, the surveyor conducted the survey at the spot of the accident and he was a licensed surveyor.
But original receipts were not produced, as such the claim of the claimant was not considered by the tribunal.
The claimant got his vehicle repaired on 24.12.2018 and the total charge of repair is Rs.2,07,777/-.

The tribunal further discussed in paragraph No.17 in detail and stated that, the estimate is for Rs.3,81,854/- towards approximate cost of the repair, but the assessment as mentioned by the surveyor for repair is Rs.1,87,412/-.
But the surveyor was not examined.
Therefore, an amount of Rs.2,30,000/- was awarded.
The claimant herein has failed to examine the surveyor.
The assessment made by the surveyor is at Ex.P.10.

In fact, the surveyor himself estimated the amount as Rs.1,87,412/-, but the actual expenses incurred by the claimant herein is Rs.2,07,777/-, as such the tribunal has NC: 2025:KHC-K:6575 HC-KAR rightly awarded a sum of Rs.2,30,000/- and this Court finds no reason to interfere with the said order.
4. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that, the amount awarded by the tribunal has already been deposited before the tribunal.
5. In view of the foregoing reasons, the appeal is dismissed.
